BiblicalUsage: Twice, always of the crown. Mark says the soldiers platted a crown of thorns and put it about His head; and John shows Jesus coming out wearing it, with Pilate's words, Behold the man!
TheologicalSignificance: An adjective that exists only for one crown carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is John's behold the man, the King wearing the curse.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
